answer: Two-path neighborhood closure requires each joining agent to show two disjoint short routes into a stable core, so a sybil cluster cannot share one gateway. Every fake identity therefore needs its own live edge node with a distinct routing table, bandwidth, and latency budget—a real hosting cost per identity. That topology signal separates a true oasis of reachable peers from a ledge of isolated clones, while the core kernel refuses any node whose routes collapse to a single path.
